chapter_title: Concerning why if a [Nail] is cut the Person shall
spiritual_reading:
You understand that the outward level of a person is like the ultimate plane in which spiritual things take fixed form, and that the powers of that outward level are like the varied perceptions and faculties that rise within it. In that ultimate plane there are many kinds of such faculties.

Some arise from interior life, renew themselves from within, and are made stable in use; they do not lose their capacity for restoration. Others, when they are deprived of what sustains them, do not return, because they have no inward root in living truth; they appear for a time from external stimulation, and when that is removed they cease. There are also mixed states that seem to recover after loss, because something of inward life still remains, and there are states that, once broken, cannot be restored, because they were never joined to what is living.

So too with the outward self: when it is allowed to take delight in what is defiled, it grows strong in disorder and draws its vitality from what is unclean, not from the Divine. Then the outward life becomes corrupted; and this corruption does not remain isolated, but spreads into what should be living in the person, so that the faculties meant to be healthy are infected, and the person’s spiritual life becomes weakened and sick. Parts of this teaching are unclear where the text is broken, but its drift is that restoration depends on whether a faculty is rooted in inward life, and that impurity in the outward self corrupts and sickens what should live.

fills.notes: The sense requires the limbs to be included as part of the body’s likeness to earth; simplest restoration is the coordination “also”.
Varieties “of” tree is the fixed natural correspondence for diverse faculties rising in the ultimate plane.
Correspondentially, what makes a faculty recover is an inward root in living ground; in the natural image this is the root in the earth.
Matches the class of states that, once cut off, do not return; the contrast requires “shall not grow again”.
These are the externally-stimulated growths that spring up and return while conditions last; reeds are a common natural image for such unstable vitality rooted in wetness rather than firm ground.
The sequence needs: cut and grow “again”, i.e., apparent recovery while a supporting medium remains.
Introduces a further distinct class in the series (recovering, not recovering, mixed, not recoverable).
Keeps the correspondence in the ultimate plane: the occurrences are “upon the earth”, i.e., in the outward level where such faculties appear.

fills.fill: like the dry trees that neither
fills.notes: The opposite class must be those without living moisture, i.e., no inward life; “dry trees” fits the correspondence for states without living truth.
Completes the natural image required by the spiritual sense: they neither grow nor produce new life after being cut.
Correspondentially the delight is in impurity; the oldest layer states the structural fact (delight in defilement) without exhortation.
Carries the idea: the outward level grows powerful in disorder when it takes pleasure in impurity.
The corruption ‘grows’ by taking in sustaining influx from an unclean source; “nourishment” fits the tree-body correspondence.
Restores the needed transition: corruption in the outer flesh does not stay isolated but spreads into what should be living.
Completes the consequence: infected faculties meant to live become weakened, hence “somewhat sick”.

assessment: Most gaps are constrained by the sustained correspondence body:earth and limbs:trees, and by the required series of four tree-types (regenerative, non-regenerative, seemingly regenerative, irrecoverable). Exact botanical terms are least constrained (notably #8), but the structural logic of inward root versus external stimulation tightly governs the restorations.
